text: The dashboard and the factory keep a busy queue simple to work through. With six Go rebuilds and copythis-ad#36 waiting at once, a proposal at the hash of the lock it amends now says "No statement changes" on its card, since that's all there is to check. On `/act` the owner can ratify every such rebuild with one confirmation, and each still posts its own ratify on its own issue. Cards list the longest wait first. An amendment of a project ratified by hand names its decision, where the card had said "#NaN". A failed build's card gives both ways on: fix the code and retry, or close the draft and draft again. An issue whose person has acted, but which the factory hasn't reached yet, shows as queued rather than waiting on a person. The factory now records a failed build's pull request being closed or merged, the protocol's `OthersClose` and `OthersMerge` steps, which it had taken only for a pull request it was still watching. So #36 couldn't go on after its draft was closed. A revise it can't take yet now says how to go on, and a pull request closed without merging waits on a person on the dashboard until someone drafts again.
